question: Let '$\mathbb{N}$' be set of all natural numbers. '$R$' be a relation on $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$: $(a,b) R (c,d) \leftrightarrow ad(b+c) = bc(a+d)$. Check if '$R$' is equivalence on $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$.
explanation:
The relation is defined by $(a,b)R(c,d)$ if $ad(b+c) = bc(a+d)$.

Reflexive: For $(a,b)$, we have $ad(b+c)$ becomes $ab(a+b)$ and $bc(a+d)$ becomes $ab(a+b)$. Hence $(a,b)R(a,b)$ and the relation is reflexive.

Symmetric: If $(a,b)R(c,d)$ then $ad(b+c)=bc(a+d)$. Interchanging the pairs gives $cb(d+a)=da(c+b)$ which is the same equality. Hence the relation is symmetric.

Transitive: Suppose $(a,b)R(c,d)$ and $(c,d)R(e,f)$. From these relations we cannot necessarily derive $af(b+e)=be(a+f)$. Thus the required equality does not always hold.

Hence the relation is not transitive.

Therefore $R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive, so it is not an equivalence relation.

options.A: $R$ is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; hence it is an equivalence relation
options.B: $R$ is not reflexive, but it is symmetric and transitive; hence it is not an equivalence relation
options.C: $R$ is reflexive and transitive but not symmetric; hence it is not an equivalence relation
options.D: $R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive; hence it is not an equivalence relation
